adj.justification: Both terms represent recorder attribution, though FAIReSheets targets the dataset level using concatenated text names while DwC:recordedBy targets an occurrence using an agent IRI.
adj.transformation_note: Requires resolving textual names to agent IRIs and mapping dataset-level creators to occurrence-level recorders.

adj.justification: The subject recordedBy refers to names of people responsible for a dataset, while the candidate datasetName refers to the title of a source dataset.
recordedBy pertains to the names of people responsible for a dataset or recording, whereas previousIdentifications records previous taxonomic name assignments for an organism.
recordedBy captures the names of people responsible for the dataset, whereas verbatimIdentification records the original taxonomic identification string.

FAIReSheets:recordedBy records the names of people responsible for a dataset, whereas DwC:taxonFormula describes a formula pattern for constructing taxonomic identifications. The concepts are completely unrelated.

FAIReSheets:recordedByID identifies agents responsible for a submitted dataset, whereas DwC:recordedByID identifies agents recording a specific occurrence. Both represent person/agent identifiers using ORCID URIs.
adj.transformation_note: Split concatenated ORCID lists on the pipe separator to map individual identifiers or align delimiter formatting with DwC guidelines.

adj.justification: FAIReSheets:recordedByID identifies people responsible for recording or submitting the dataset, whereas DwC:identifiedByID identifies the agent who made the taxonomic identification.
adj.transformation_note: Splitting or merging pipe-separated lists of ORCIDs may be needed depending on system requirements.

adj.justification: recordedByID refers to identifiers for people responsible for a dataset, whereas previousIdentifications refers to historical taxonomic assignments for an organism.
FAIReSheets recordedByID identifies the people (e.g., ORCID) responsible for the dataset, whereas DwC datasetID identifies the dataset itself.
recordedByID refers to global identifiers for people responsible for data collection or submission, whereas identificationID is a unique identifier for a taxonomic identification event.
Subject refers to contact details (e.g., email address) for a project contact person, whereas Candidate refers to unique identifiers for the project itself.

The subject field project_contact refers to contact details for data inquiries, whereas DwC:projectTitle represents the titles or names of contributing projects. These fields represent entirely different metadata concepts.
The subject project_contact specifies contact information (such as an email address) for project enquiries, whereas organismInteractionID is an identifier for a biological organism interaction.
The subject specifies the institution name or entity having custody, whereas the candidate specifically requires a unique identifier for the organization.
adj.transformation_note: Requires looking up and resolving the institution name to an organization identifier such as a ROR ID.

adj.justification: Both fields identify the entity having custody of the record or resource. FAIReSheets institution emphasizes the full institutional name, whereas DwC institutionCode specifically expects an acronym or code.
adj.transformation_note: Convert or lookup full institution names to their corresponding institutional acronyms or codes.

adj.justification: The subject refers to an organization holding custody of an object or record, while the candidate refers to a branch of knowledge.
FAIReSheets:institution refers to the organization holding custody of a record or object, whereas DwC:basisOfRecord indicates the specific nature or type of the data record.
The subject term refers to an institution having custody of a record or object, while the candidate term identifies the source establishing a relationship between two resources.

The candidate broadly defines an identifier for any organization, whereas the subject specifically restricts it to the institution having custody of the record's object or information. Both accept identical persistent identifier URI formats such as ROR IDs.

Both concepts identify the institution having custody of the resource, but FAIReSheets:institutionID requires a persistent identifier (e.g., ROR URI) while DwC:institutionCode expects an acronym or textual code.
adj.transformation_note: Map persistent identifiers (e.g., ROR URLs) to institutional acronyms/codes using an institutional registry or lookup table.

adj.justification: FAIReSheets:institutionID represents a persistent identifier for the institution holding custody, whereas DwC:ownerInstitutionCode represents a code or acronym for the institution holding ownership. They differ in both concept focus (custody vs. ownership) and expected format (resolvable URI vs. acronym).
adj.transformation_note: Requires mapping institutional acronyms to persistent identifiers (such as ROR or ISNI URIs) and resolving potential differences between owner and custodian institutions.
